name: Morgan Stanley
business_model: Other (investment banking, trading and wealth fees on top of a balance sheet)

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Global investment bank plus a very large wealth franchise: Wealth Management (WM) $10.5T client assets (WM + Investment Mgmt), trading/advisory, asset management; 84k staff, 42 countries.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: FY2025 net revenue $70.6B: Institutional Securities (IS) $33.1B (47%), WM $31.8B (45%), Investment Mgmt (IM) $6.5B (9%) before eliminations. YTD 2026 pre-tax: IS ~57%, WM ~38%, IM ~5% (derived from segment revenue x margin, so earnings are NOT mostly wealth).

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Wealthy individuals and workplace plan participants (WM), corporates, funds and governments (IS), institutions (IM); highly diffuse, no top-customer concentration disclosed; IS clients are cyclical (Equity revenue $5.8B in 3Q, +41%).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Americas is the core; Asia net revenue +55% in 3Q on equities, EMEA -6%; FX exposure not quantified in the sources read; wealth clients are mainly US.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Fee on client assets (WM asset management $5.5B of $9.1B in 3Q, 61%), net interest income (WM $2.2B), plus transaction/trading and deal fees. WM fee-based assets $3,155B. Roughly half of firm revenue is recurring or asset-linked; the other half is market-activity driven.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Efficiency ratio 67% in 3Q, 66% YTD; compensation $8.0B is largely variable (payout to advisors rises with revenue). Non-comp expenses +20% yoy on execution and tech. Capex-light; the balance sheet is the working capital (total assets $1.69T, +19% since Dec 2025). Guidance: ROTCE goal 20%, delivered 25.4% YTD.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs are funding and capital, not goods. Deposits $478B (WM sweep and savings, the sticky input; cost 2.51% period-end at Dec 2025), wholesale funding (borrowings $389B) tied to hy_spreads/fed_funds tags, regulatory capital (CET1 14.9% vs 11.8% required; tag regulation), advisors and tech vendors (wages, software_capex tags). Pass-through: WM deposit costs reprice with Fed funds; trading funding costs hit 'Other' IS revenue (3Q higher funding cost). HY OAS 3.72% (+105bp since Aug) raises issuance cost but MS has no single supplier chokepoint; main single point of failure is dependence on wholesale funding markets and prime-broker/clearing access in stress.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale in both advice and markets: $232B net new assets in 3Q (just over half IPO-related) and $80B fee-based flows; Integrated Firm links IS clients to WM. Doing differently now: lending growth in WM (loans $201B vs $174B), workplace channel, new corporate retirement mandate.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Known brand to wealthy households and via E*TRADE to retail; not a daily consumer brand and clients would notice but could switch advisors. Switching costs are real for advisor-led accounts. Marketing and business development costs rose in 3Q.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: JPM, BAC/Merrill, GS, UBS, Schwab, Wells. WM net new assets 2025 $356B (2024 $252B, 2023 $282B) and pre-tax margin 30.4% in 3Q (29% FY25, 27% FY24) suggest share gains; IM long-term flows +$15.8B but IM revenue -12% on carry reversal.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Client assets $10.5T; fee-based assets $3.16T up 19% yoy; WM loans +16% yoy; workplace and self-directed funnels. Limiting: 3Q net new assets inflated by IPO flows, and 3Q equity trading may be a peak.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 22.6% (3Q), 25.4% YTD vs ~10% cost of equity; $4.8B buybacks YTD at avg $212.74 in 3Q (stock now $167.55, so bought higher), new $20B authorization June 2026; dividend raised to $1.15. Bank: FCF not the right measure. CEO pay 96% variable, 100% of deferred in PSUs tied to returns; insider ownership % not extracted.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Wealth and asset management gaining relevance; trading and deal revenues are cyclical. Risks: market decline cuts asset fees with lag (asset management is 61% of WM revenue), key-person (CEO Pick), tokenization and fee compression, IS earnings concentration. Level 3 asset valuation is the critical audit matter.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 4.01/4.02 or NT filings since 2023; Deloitte clean opinion on financials and internal controls (FY2025); March 2026 CORRESP is a routine S-3 acceleration request. Flags: Nov 20 2026 8-K changes carried-interest accounting retroactively (cumulative -$719M retained earnings, change in principle, not a restatement); E*TRADE class actions (since 2024); $178M severance in 1Q.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: positive (WM NII, strong trading, deal activity) but a Fed hike raises deposit and funding costs. Slowdown: asset fees fall with markets and IS revenues drop, partly offset by sticky net new assets. Stagflation: negative. Dollar up is a mild headwind to non-US revenue; 10y 4.85% helps WM spread but weighs on bond marks.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Capital: SCB 4.3% locked through Dec 31 2027 under Sept 30 2026 final rule; G-SIB surcharge 3.0% with Mar 2026 proposal pending; Basel III proposal pending. Currently favourable direction but headline risk. SLR 4.8% and leverage ratio 5.9% are the tighter limits than CET1.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $167.55 (2026-11-25 close) / TBV $53.96 = 3.10x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth, P/TBV 3.10 needs sustained ROTCE of ~24.7% (g+(CoE-g)*P/TBV). Actual ROTCE 22.6% 3Q, 25.4% YTD, 21.6% FY25, firm goal 20%. At 20% fair P/TBV is 2.43x (~$131, -22%); at 22.6% 2.80x (~$151). P/E ~13.3x on TTM EPS ~$12.61 vs year-end P/E 10.4x (2021), 12.2x (2022), 16.5x (2023), 15.0x (2024), 17.0x (2025). Peer JPM 2.81x TBV ($316.74/$112.64) at ROTCE ~21%. Own 5-year P/TBV range not computed (no TBV history pulled). Price is down 21% in 3m but still assumes peak-like returns, so no cushion.

status_reason: Quality is good but price/tangible book of 3.1x already needs ~25% ROTCE forever, and earnings are majority Institutional Securities (YTD pre-tax ~57%), so the wealth-misread premise does not hold.

feedback.note: MS wealth: record 3Q fee-based flows $80B and NNA $232B (over half IPO-related) confirm client activity and strong markets in the hard data; IS Equity +41% confirms high volumes; trading-driven earnings peak risk matches the market's Slowdown read.
